original_question: Is there a sufficiently simple and flexible way to realize the generalized theta functions in H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) as holomorphic functions, analogous to how classical theta functions describe sections of O(kΘ) on a Jacobian?
target_in_paper: §10, Q 9 ("Are there generalized theta functions?"): Beauville asks whether there is a sufficiently simple and flexible way of expressing the elements of H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) as holomorphic functions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official question. It keeps the key phrases "sufficiently simple and flexible," "H^0(SU_X(r), L^k)," and "as holomorphic functions," and it correctly frames the problem by analogy with the classical Jacobian and its theta functions. It also uses the paper’s terminology that sections of L^k are generalized theta functions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
missing_details: The draft should identify X as a compact Riemann surface over C; Beauville also says he will usually assume g ≥ 2 in what follows, since the cases g ≤ 1 are easy and exceptional. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
SU_X(r) should be defined explicitly as the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

The line bundle L should be defined as the determinant line bundle O(Θ_L), where Θ_L = {E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X, E ⊗ L) ≥ 1} for L in J^{g-1}(X), and this line bundle is independent of the choice of L. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

The quantifier k ≥ 1 should be made explicit. The paper discusses the problem for the spaces H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) in general, not only for k = 1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

Because the paper says the missing phenomenon is in higher rank, it is better to indicate that the intended nontrivial range is r ≥ 2; for rank 1 the classical theta-function picture is already known. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, one should say that the desired holomorphic functions are to live on some natural explicit auxiliary complex space attached to SU_X(r), not on SU_X(r) itself; §10 discusses possible models via the double quotient/central extension from §7 and via pullback to SL_r(C)^g. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

The phrase "sufficiently simple and flexible" should remain intentionally informal: Beauville explicitly presents Q 9 as a loosely formulated question, so the rewrite should not replace it by a stronger formal requirement that the paper itself does not impose. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let L be its determinant line bundle. For a given integer k ≥ 1 (in the genuinely non-Abelian case r ≥ 2), is there a sufficiently simple and flexible way to express the generalized theta functions H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) as holomorphic functions on some natural explicit auxiliary complex space attached to SU_X(r), analogous to the classical realization of H^0(J_X, O(kΘ)) by theta functions on a Jacobian? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Beauville’s Q 9 in §10, not the earlier questions about base loci, embeddings, Verlinde-type dimensions, or strange duality. The decisive cue is that Beauville says the missing higher-rank ingredient is an analytic description of sections as holomorphic functions and then asks, in nearly the same words as your draft, whether such a simple and flexible expression exists. The surrounding discussion explains why the question is subtle: classical theta theory does not extend directly because SU_X(r) is simply connected, and Beauville only points to tentative constructions via the stack-theoretic double quotient/central extension and via pullback to SL_r(C)^g. The notation H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) and the terminology "generalized theta functions" come from the earlier definition of the determinant bundle L. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
